comment: Values approximate; verify against NASA sources.
notes: data_rate_bps is the generated rate while operating (null for film, which returns physically). science_value is 1-4 stars.

instruments.name: Radiation counter (Geiger)
instruments.description: Cheap and classic. Counts charged particles; shows the Van Allen belts.
instruments.source: Inspired by the real Geiger counter on Explorer 1 (1958), used by James Van Allen's team.

instruments.name: Magnetometer
instruments.description: Measures magnetic fields. Needs a boom, which adds mass.
instruments.source: Inspired by the real fluxgate magnetometers flown on Explorer 10 and Pioneer probes, 1960-61.

instruments.name: Micrometeorite detector
instruments.description: Counts dust impacts to size up the hazard for future crews.
instruments.source: Inspired by the real micrometeoroid detectors on Explorer 1 and Explorer 16, 1958-62.

instruments.name: Film camera
instruments.description: High-quality pictures, but the film canister must come home in a return capsule.
instruments.source: Inspired by the real film capsules of the Corona / Discoverer reconnaissance satellites, 1960.

instruments.name: TV camera
instruments.description: Live pictures, but they eat comms bandwidth and power.
instruments.source: Inspired by the real TIROS-1 TV cameras (1960) and Ranger probe cameras, 1960s.

instruments.name: Spectrometer
instruments.description: Reads the chemical makeup of light from planets, atmospheres and surfaces.
instruments.source: Inspired by the real ultraviolet and infrared spectrometers on Mariner probes, 1960s.

instruments.name: Surface sampler (Moon)
instruments.description: Scoops and analyses lunar soil. Needs a successful landing.
instruments.source: Inspired by the real Surveyor 3 soil mechanics surface sampler, 1967.
